title: SDK assets and configuration
prerequisites: Required: run sdk_native_preflight against the selected environment before building or activation. Native KSSIDP uses BDDKEnrollment/BDDKLogin, useTokenBasedLogin=true, astServerBackend=maverick and login header X-KOBIL-ASTUSERID. The WebView alternative is KSTrustedWebView with explicit deployment clients. Missing clients or incompatible bindings block progress; never create substitute flows.
These bindings target classic MCSDK with KSSIDP; standalone IDPSDK needs its own adapter and is not interchangeable.
Select Shift SDK family, mobile SDK artifact version and native platform.
Obtain authorized SDK binaries and a matching server application/version with registration user selected.
Supply backend-issued SDK configuration and trust/configuration assets; keep backend admin credentials out of the app.

Local toolchain preflight BEFORE long builds: a COMPLETELY installed Android NDK for the selected version (source.properties and toolchain binaries present, not merely listed), supported compiler versions, iOS deployment target validated against the installed Xcode minimum, signing/provisioning and physical-device readiness, and free disk space. An unsupported or half-installed toolchain must be a precise preflight finding, never a mid-build surprise. Never mutate shared toolchains (SDK/NDK installs, global Xcode settings) automatically; report the finding to the owner (2026-09-29 validation round, VAL-06/VAL-07).
sequence:
## Mobile identity and AST registration

Android applicationId and iOS bundle identifier are mobile application identities.
AST app_name and its registered version identify backend registration records;
they are not automatically the same identifier. A new mobile bundle ID alone
neither proves an existing AST registration is incompatible nor proves it reusable.
Never recommend adopting the SuperApp mobile bundle ID just to reuse its assets.

For an authorized app integration, proceed with sdk_app_list, sdk_app_get and
sdk_app_versions without asking for another confirmation for these read-only
checks. Inspect the selected platform/version, registration user, lock state,
integrity policy, and any signing/package binding required by the supplied SDK
and deployment. If returned metadata cannot establish a required binding, identify
that exact gap; do not claim compatibility from the app name or integrity flag alone.
Reuse a suitable existing app/version and preserve its registration user and
security policy. Create new records only when none is suitable or the user requests
separate registration. Do not disable integrity to force reuse.

Do not assert that a delivered sdk_config.jwt is bound to a mobile package or AST
app/version without inspecting the documented configuration contract and applicable
claims privately. sdk_config_write in this MCP takes certificates and connection
service settings, not a mobile bundle ID or AST app_name. Obtain a fresh
backend-signed configuration when required; never edit signed JWT contents.

Preserve the user's previously selected test security policy and flow. Ask only
for an unresolved binding/policy choice or an actual blocker; do not request the
same decision repeatedly. A test selection is not a default for other customers.

## Signed configuration and retained choices
Within an authorized app build, request a fresh signed SDK configuration with
sdk_config_write using the selected environment service map and verified public
TLS certificates. Do not ask the user to supply a JWT or propose trying an
unverified sample JWT when the MCP can issue one. If certificates, permissions
or services are missing, report that concrete prerequisite; never disable TLS
verification or edit a signed configuration.
Read project instructions (including CLAUDE.md when present) for previously
selected test policy before asking again. Reuse an explicit current-project
ALLOW_VIRTUAL_SMART_CARD/device-PIN decision; do not extend that test choice to
other projects. This does not authorize changing shared backend security policy.
Inspect supplied release manifest and archive layout; inventory framework/AAR dependencies and architectures.

## Release-qualified mc_config/app_config structure (verified 2026-09-29 validation round, Android MCSDK 15.16.3088426 / iOS MCSDK 15.16.803.3089231)

The delivered mc_config for this qualified tuple contains: useScp, useTokenBasedLogin,
useSmartScreen, astServerBackend, an iam object {clientId, serverUrl (origin only,
no path), redirectUri, trustedSslServerCerts} and a maverick object {mTLS, mKex,
useSEKeyForSigningTransactions}. Configuration assets (mc_config/app_config
templates) come from the delivery's GettingStarted asset ZIPs, not from the
framework/xcframework archive (the iOS xcframeworks ZIP contains none). Fill
values from the selected deployment; never invent keys or copy another
deployment's values. Other releases require their own qualification.

The SDK configuration category/tag is NOT the TMS notification category. For
deployments without that configuration, leaving BOTH category and tag empty is
correct. Mapping the TMS notification category into the SDK configuration
category with an empty tag caused FatalError ScpParameterError 800000133
("Tag is empty, but category not") and a failed Start (runtime-verified,
2026-09-29 validation round).
Add SDK libraries and required assets to the app target/package.
Load the selected configuration from the actual runtime bundle/assets directory. Fail with an actionable missing-file error.
Pass the configuration, backend type and trust material to the version-specific SDK start API.

## Trust anchors from mobile-negotiated chains (verified 2026-09-29, Android MCSDK 15.16.3088426 / iOS MCSDK 15.16.803.3089231)

Derive approved trust anchors (mc_config iam.trustedSslServerCerts for SDK Start;
the separate WebView trust input for the trusted WebView) from the certificate
chains ACTUALLY negotiated by the mobile TLS clients, not from a desktop TLS
check alone: iOS builds Let's Encrypt chains to the self-signed system root
ISRG Root X2 while desktop verification sees ISRG Root X1 via the cross-sign.
Pin the fingerprint-checked authentic X2 alongside X1 when both can appear.
Match each API's expected DER/PEM contract, never hard-code one CA for all
environments, and NEVER disable certificate or hostname verification. For iOS,
package AND explicitly pass the IAM certificate chain at Start.

Before any device run, compare the served chains against the prepared trust
asset with sdk_tls_chain_check: it fetches each host's actually-served chain,
reports subject/issuer/SHA-256 per certificate and names the MISSING anchors
(verified evidence 2026-09-29: akinci served leaf<-YE2<-Root YE<-ISRG Root X2
with X2 cross-signed by X1; an X1-only asset is reported as missing X2 -
VAL-16/VAL-36, two device rounds lost). The check makes no trust decision and
never replaces or weakens the app's own verification.
expected_result: Required assets exist in the installed application, not just the project directory.
checklist: Required assets exist in the installed application, not just the project directory.
Backend app name/version/platform agree with runtime start parameters.
SDK version is identified from artifacts/runtime information, not the MCP release number.
Mobile bundle/package identity and AST app/version are distinguished; reuse decision is supported by registration, integrity and applicable binding evidence.

mc_config/app_config are sourced from the delivery's GettingStarted asset ZIPs and match the release-qualified key structure; missing template assets were flagged before scaffolding (structure verified 2026-09-29 validation round, Android MCSDK 15.16.3088426 / iOS MCSDK 15.16.803.3089231).
Trust anchors verified against actually-negotiated mobile chains per platform; SDK Start trust and WebView trust configured and tested separately.

Local toolchain preflight completed before the first long build: complete NDK installation, supported compiler versions, iOS deployment target vs installed Xcode, signing/device readiness and disk space; physical-device checks recorded separately from simulator checks.
failure_handling: Do not invent fixed asset filenames or copy a customer endpoint from an example.
Missing or mismatched SDK configuration can fail before activation; record start result and error events.
Never disable useTokenBasedLogin to work around ast_login_with_unactivated_client; this skips IAM setup and can cause CannotAcquireTokenData(50). Investigate the selected native backend flow instead.

Swift: switch on KssIdpStatus.success/eventFailed/requestFailed; never infer success from text containing accept. Preserve detailed callback status, errorCode and underlying event without logging tokens or credentials.

800000133 FatalError ScpParameterError "Tag is empty, but category not": the SDK configuration category/tag is not the TMS notification category. Both empty is the correct choice for deployments without that configuration (runtime-verified, 2026-09-29 validation round, Android MCSDK 15.16.3088426 / iOS MCSDK 15.16.803.3089231).

800000015 SCP_ERROR_CANNOT_READ_APP_CONFIG is emitted as a warning on Start and Start can still succeed (runtime-verified on Android 15.16.3088426, 2026-09-29 validation round). Whether app_config is required or optional for a given deployment is only partially unverified/unconfirmed; preserve the warning and investigate instead of asserting either semantic or silently ignoring it.

800000279 ("Signed jwt together with mkex or SE for signing transactions is not supported yet", Start NOT_SUPPORTED): this release rejects SignedJWT login combined with maverick.mKex=true or useSEKeyForSigningTransactions=true. The tested known-good SignedJWT combination on this tuple used mKex=false and useSEKeyForSigningTransactions=false (runtime-verified, 2026-09-29 validation round). Record of a tested combination, not a universal default for other releases or deployment policies.

KS_CERTIFICATE_ERROR at the trusted WebView (onURLBlocked reason 1, subsystem 1500000, "servercert validation endresult failed") while SDK Start succeeds: WebView pinning did not cover the mobile-negotiated chain; SDK Start trust and WebView trust are separate inputs. Verified fix 2026-09-29: pin ISRG Root X2 (system root store, fingerprint-checked) alongside X1. Diagnose with KsTrustedWebView.setLogListener and temporary KsTwvLog.setLogLevel(debug). Never blank-fail the WebView (VAL-36, 2026-09-29): the X1-only pinning failure on Flutter iOS rendered a SILENT white/blank page with no user-visible error, and the gap was only found by chain inspection. In the reference integration a blank page must be IMPOSSIBLE: wire onWebResourceError/onWebResourceHttpError (Flutter NavigationDelegate), the trusted-WebView failure callbacks (onURLBlocked/KS_CERTIFICATE_ERROR, load-failure delegate methods) and every TLS-failure path to a visible in-app diagnostic view that replaces the WebView content and shows the numeric error code, the phase and a sanitized hint (for example 'certificate validation failed - check the pinned trust anchors'), never URLs, hostnames, tokens or other secrets. Surfacing the error never means weakening or disabling validation. Tests must force a trust failure and assert the diagnostic view appears instead of a blank page.

Half-installed Android NDK (VAL-06, 2026-09-29): a selected NDK 26.3 without complete toolchain contents failed mid-build. The build then compiled with the locally installed NDK 27.2.12479018 - record such a switch as a LOCAL WORKAROUND, not vendor qualification of the SDK/NDK combination, and keep the vendor-supported combination question open. Detect incompleteness in preflight, and do not auto-install or modify shared NDK/SDK components.

iOS deployment target below the installed Xcode's minimum (VAL-07, 2026-09-29): the Flutter Runner/Pods target had to be raised to iOS 15 for Xcode 27, discovered only during compilation. Validate app and Pods deployment targets against the current Xcode before long builds and record the actual toolchain/SDK minimums.

platform_notes.android: Android AssetReader is used to load mc configuration and SDK configuration bytes. Constructor signatures and filenames must match the supplied release. If a bundled AAR declares application@label, resolve the manifest merger conflict explicitly (for example tools:replace="android:label" on your app label).
platform_notes.ios: The inspected Swift start path uses KSMStartEventEx with serverBackend, ssmsAppConfiguration, mcConfig, certificateChain and configurationData. Bundle target membership matters. MCSDK 15.16 KSMasterController dynamically depends on hnb.framework: embed and sign both supplied xcframeworks. A successful link alone does not prove launch readiness. Live startup required the designated initializer with explicit iamCertificateChain, followed by serverBackend assignment. Omitting the IAM chain caused FatalError 800000174 (chain absent from SDK database) even though the certificate was packaged.

qualification.note: Examples compile against the exact classic MCSDK/KSSIDP artifact in each example validation record. Compilation and synthetic diagnostics do not qualify a complete live app flow.
